business_quality.justification: Genuinely excellent economics: operating margin 32.8%, FCF margin 33.8%, and $9.09B of free cash flow on $26.9B revenue. Asset-light marketplace with negative working capital. Q2 2026 delivered 5% room-night growth to 325 million, 9% gross-bookings growth to $51.0B, and $3.64B of quarterly FCF (+16%). Deducted because the six-year growth figures are badly distorted - FY2020 revenue of $6.8B was the covid travel trough, so the headline 31.7% revenue CAGR and 146.8% net-income CAGR measure recovery, not growth. On the recent three years the real rate is ~16%, and the latest years were +11% and +13%.

competitive_advantage.justification: A real two-sided network: more properties attract more travellers which attract more properties, reinforced by enormous brand-search spend and supplier habit. Booking.com's European hotel supply is difficult to replicate. Deducted 2 points for genuine structural threats - Google inserting itself between traveller and OTA, hotel direct-booking pushes, and the fact that a large share of traffic is rented through paid marketing rather than owned.

catalysts.justification: Dated and specific: Q3 2026 guidance of 3-5% room-night growth and 4-6% growth in gross bookings, revenue and adjusted EBITDA, with full-year adjusted EPS growth guided to the low-to-mid teens. The mechanical catalyst is capital return - $4.1B returned in Q2 2026 including $3.7B of buybacks, the largest quarterly return in company history, against a share count already down 20.7%. Marked down because guidance points to DECELERATION, and management explicitly flags continued indirect impacts from the Middle East conflict.

risk_reward.justification: Base case +17% against a bear case of -33%. Travel is discretionary and highly cyclical: a consumer recession hits room nights, take rate and marketing efficiency simultaneously. The valuation already embeds a good outcome at 25x earnings and 14.9x free cash flow, so this is not a discounted entry. Weak asymmetry.

management.justification: Aggressive, consistent buybacks have cut the share count 20.7% and genuinely compound per-share value. But two deductions. First, shareholders' equity is NEGATIVE $5.6B from buying back stock beyond retained earnings, which removes the ROIC check entirely and reduces the buffer in a downturn. Second, insider behaviour is one-sided: 55 open-market sales and ZERO purchases across the Form 4 filings examined, netting -$33.3M. That is not proof of anything - most will be scheduled 10b5-1 plans - but zero buys at any price is a fact worth recording.
